hints: Focus on what 'filled' really means for first ionisation, it means the electron leaves an orbital that holds two electrons, not just a full subshell.
Write out the Period 3 outer configurations from Na ($3s^1$) to Ar ($3s^2 3p^6$) and remember Hund's rule keeps $p$ electrons unpaired until $3p^4$.
Check which elements actually lose a paired electron, Mg from its $3s^2$ pair and S, Cl, Ar from a doubly occupied $3p$ orbital, then match the list.
walkthrough:
**Recall what first ionisation removes**

Think side by side with me. First ionisation always removes the outermost electron from the gaseous atom.

$$\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^+\text{(g)} + \text{e}^-$$

**Write the outer electron arrangements**

For Na to Ar the inner $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6$ core is the same, so only $3s$ and $3p$ matter. Let's list them simply.

$$\text{Na: } 3s^1, \text{ Mg: } 3s^2, \text{ Al: } 3s^2 3p^1, \text{ Si: } 3s^2 3p^2$$
$$\text{P: } 3s^2 3p^3, \text{ S: } 3s^2 3p^4, \text{ Cl: } 3s^2 3p^5, \text{ Ar: } 3s^2 3p^6$$

**Apply Hund's rule to the p electrons**

An orbital is filled when it holds 2 electrons. A $p$ subshell has three orbitals, and electrons go singly into separate orbitals first.

So Al ($3p^1$), Si ($3p^2$) and P ($3p^3$) all lose a single, unpaired $p$ electron. They are not removed from a filled orbital.

**Spot the paired electrons that are lost**

Mg loses from $3s^2$, which is a filled $s$ orbital. From S onwards pairing has started, so S ($3p^4$), Cl ($3p^5$) and Ar ($3p^6$) all lose an electron from a doubly occupied $3p$ orbital.

That leaves Mg, S, Cl and Ar only.

options.A: Incorrect. This includes Al, Si and P, but those three all lose a single unpaired $3p$ electron from a half filled orbital, not a filled orbital. It also wrongly includes Na's absence but overcounts the p-block.
options.B: Incorrect. This correctly includes S, Cl and Ar but wrongly includes Al, Si and P and wrongly leaves out Mg. Al, Si and P lose unpaired electrons, while Mg loses from its filled $3s^2$ orbital and should be included.
options.C: Correct. Mg loses from filled $3s^2$. S ($3p^4$), Cl ($3p^5$) and Ar ($3p^6$) each lose from a $3p$ orbital containing two electrons due to spin pairing. Na, Al, Si and P all lose a single unpaired electron, so they are excluded.
options.D: Incorrect. S, Cl and Ar are correct because they lose a paired $3p$ electron, but Mg is missing. Students often forget that a full $s$ orbital ($3s^2$) also counts as a filled orbital.
